# `String`

The `String` type represents an immutable, length-prefixed, NUL-reserved sequence of UTF-8 encoded bytes. Strings in Edva are value types designed for high performance, memory safety, and seamless C interoperability without allocations.

## Declaration and annotations

Strings are bound with `=` or typed explicitly using `: String`:

```dva
greeting = "Hello, world!"
path: String = "/etc/edva/config.ccl"
```

## Literals and syntax

Edva supports two string literal formats:

### Standard escaped strings
Enclosed in double quotes `"..."`, supporting C-style escape sequences:

```dva
message = "First line\nSecond line\t(tabbed)\nPath: \"/usr/bin\""
```

Supported escapes include `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\0`, `\a`, `\b`, `\f`, `\v`, `\"`, `\'`, and `\\`.

### Raw strings
Enclosed in `(=` and `=)`. Raw strings contain literal bytes without escape processing (ideal for regex, embedded scripts, SQL queries, or Markdown):

```dva
raw_sql = (=
SELECT id, username, email
FROM users
WHERE status = 'active'
=)
```

The only escape sequence recognized in raw strings is `=\)`, which emits a literal `=)`.

## The `{ len, data }` fat-pointer ABI

At runtime, every `String` value is represented by a 16-byte fat pointer struct:

```dva
{ len: i64, data: ptr }
```

### The NUL-reserved contract
When a whole `String` is allocated or created from a literal, Edva guarantees that the byte immediately following the string data (`data[len]`) is a `NUL` (`\0`) byte.
This allows Edva strings to pass directly to C library APIs (like `libc::open`, `libc::printf`, or `os::stat`) using the address-of operator `&s` without copying or allocating temporary buffers.

### Generation-tagged liveness
The upper bits of the 64-bit `len` word store an arena generation tag. If an arena resets, accessing a string that belonged to an earlier generation immediately traps with runtime error `E4010` rather than causing undefined behavior or use-after-free corruption.

## Operations

### Reading string metadata

Edva deliberately avoids dot-property member access (`.len` and `.data` are compile-time errors `E3065` and `E3066`). Instead, prefix operators query string metadata:

```dva
s = "Edva Language"

// Byte length
byte_len = ?s          // 13

// Unicode codepoint count
codepoints = ??s       // 13

// Raw pointer to UTF-8 data bytes
raw_ptr = &s           // Addr / ptr
```

### Concatenation (`+`)

The binary `+` operator concatenates strings, or appends formatted scalar values:

```dva
prefix = "item_"
id = 42

key = prefix + "user"      // "item_user"
tagged = prefix + id       // "item_42" (direct integer-to-string concatenation)
```

### Slicing and indexing

Strings support sub-range slicing and indexed byte access:

```dva
text = "Antigravity"

// Substring slicing: text(start .. end)
sub = text(0 .. 4)        // "Anti"

// Indexed access produces a fallible ram < String | Error >
first_slot = text(0)      // In-bounds: <+ "A" +>
oob_slot   = text(99)     // Out-of-bounds: <- Error(4001, "Out of bounds") ->
```

### Immutability guarantee

Strings are strictly immutable. Any attempt to write into a string (`s(0) = 'B'`) or overwrite fields (`s.len = 5`) produces an immediate compile error. When mutable string accumulation is needed, use [`Builder`](builder.qmd).
